prompt: What best describes the role of vascular cambium during secondary growth in a cannabis stem?
options: It produces additional vascular tissues that contribute to radial thickening
It converts mature leaves directly into stem tissue
It is the main site of pollen production
It replaces the root system after flowering begins
explanation: Vascular cambium is a lateral meristem. As secondary growth proceeds it contributes new secondary xylem toward the inside and secondary phloem toward the outside, increasing stem thickness.

prompt: Which statement correctly compares major supporting tissues in a mature Cannabis sativa stem?
options: Bast fiber bundles occur toward the stem periphery while the inner xylem-rich core becomes more lignified
Bast fibers occur only inside the pith and xylem occurs only in the epidermis
All stem support comes from water pressure and no cell walls contribute
Bast fibers are reproductive tissues that develop only after pollination
explanation: Cannabis stems contain cellulose-rich bast fibers associated with outer phloem regions and a more lignified xylem-rich inner core. Their position, cell-wall composition, and maturation all contribute to mechanical behavior.

prompt: What is the main physical idea behind cohesion-tension transport in xylem?
options: Transpiration and water-potential gradients place a cohesive water column under tension from leaves toward roots
The stem pumps water upward using rhythmic muscle-like contractions
Phloem pressure forces all xylem water downward
Water moves upward only when roots generate positive pressure
explanation: Transpiration lowers water potential toward the leaf end of the pathway. Cohesion between water molecules and adhesion to conduit walls allow tension to be transmitted through the xylem water column.

prompt: Why can an embolized xylem conduit reduce stem hydraulic conductivity?
options: Gas occupying part of the conduit interrupts the continuous liquid pathway used for water transport
Gas permanently turns the conduit into phloem
Embolism increases the number of functioning water columns in every case
An embolized conduit immediately stops photosynthesis in every leaf on the plant
explanation: When gas fills a xylem conduit, that conduit loses part or all of its ability to conduct the continuous water column. Whole-stem impact depends on how much of the hydraulic network is affected and on plant context.
